cases.title: Correct parsing up to a potential partial boundary
cases.bug: _last_partial_boundary_index is called on the whole buffer instead of data[data_start:] (+ data_start), so it can return a newline before data_start and corrupt multipart parsing with chunked data

matched.title: Partial-boundary search ignores data_start, so the leading line break can leak into part data
matched.failure:
A part body arrives as b'
AB' in the first chunk, so the buffer is shorter than a boundary. The helper returns 0, which is below data_start 2. Data(b'', more_data=True) is emitted, nothing is deleted, and the state becomes DATA. A later chunk of 'CD...' (non-empty and long) leaves the buffer as b'
ABCD...'. The next DATA event then returns b'
ABCD...', so the value gains a spurious leading CRLF.
notes: removed evidence that does not resolve: hunk:src/werkzeug/sansio/multipart.py:243

warn_titles: src/werkzeug/sansio/multipart.py:252 Partial-boundary search ignores data_start, so the leading line break can leak into part data

cases.title: Correctly implement multipart parsing for empty fields
cases.bug: _parse_data computes data_start but calls last_newline() over the whole buffer, whose leading CRLF makes the last newline index 0, and the find() shortcut is gone so each chunk runs a full regex: large multipart bodies parse wrongly and slowly

matched.title: Leading line break leaks into field data when body arrives without a boundary in the first chunk
matched.failure: Field headers end with a blank line and the next chunk is b"longer than the boundary". The buffer is b"\r\nlonger than the boundary", so `last_newline()` is 0. The first Data is empty and nothing is deleted. After the boundary arrives, the field value is b"\r\nlonger than the boundary...", which has a spurious leading CRLF. Any streamed upload whose first chunk lacks a trailing newline gets corrupted. The chunked test only checks isinstance, so it misses this.
notes: removed evidence that does not resolve: ref:tests/sansio/test_multipart.py:70

warn_titles: src/werkzeug/sansio/multipart.py:265 Leading line break leaks into field data when body arrives without a boundary in the first chunk

cases.title: Added HandleContext to re-enter soft-rewritten Requests. (#709)
cases.bug: HandleContext resets the context (handlers and index) and re-enters routing without restoring them, so the original chain continues on the new route's handlers and middleware re-runs; it also returns c to the pool while still in use

matched.title: reset() while the outer handler chain is still running
matched.failure: After a middleware calls HandleContext and returns, the outer Next loop sees the index left by the inner run and may skip the remaining handlers or run them again. Keys set before the call are lost.
notes: removed evidence that does not resolve: ref:gin.go:269

severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading did not confirm the failing case (Resetting the context and running the full routing again is what re-entering a rewritten request means. After the inner run the index is past the end of the new handler chain, so the outer Next loop simply stops. Losing Keys and the chain state is the fresh-request semantics the doc comment announce)
